newsitem.title: USA: Western Bancorp, Santa Monica Bank merge.
newsitem.headline: Western Bancorp, Santa Monica Bank merge.

text.p: Western Bancorp and Santa Monica Bank said Thursday they had signed a definitive agreement to merge.
Under the deal, Santa Monica shareholders can choose to receive either $28 cash per share, or 0.875 share of Western Bancorp common for each Santa Monica Bank share.
If holders of more than 50 percent of Santa Monica's common stock choose to receive Western Bancorp stock, shares and cash will be distributed on a pro rata basis.

If holders of less than 40 percent of the outstanding Santa Monica shares choose to receive stock, all shareholders will receive $28 cash per share at closing, the companies said in a joint statement.
Santa Monica Bank and Western Bank, a Western Bancorp unit, will merge operations, forming a $1.1 billion bank operating in western Los Angeles under the Santa Monica Bank name.
Western Bancorp then will have two subsidiaries: Santa Monica Bank and National Bank of Southern California.
National Bank will merge into Southern California Bank after Western's previously announced acquisition of its parent, SC Bancorp, is completed.
Aubrey Austin, chief executive of Santa Monica Bank, will become chairman, president and CEO of the merged Santa Monica Bank, and a director of Western Bancorp.
Western Bancorp Chairman Hugh Smith and President Matthew Wagner will continue in those positions. Mark Stuenkel, president of National Bank of Southern California, also will continue in that job.

Upon the expected completion of the merger in January 1998, Western Bancorp will have assets of roughly $2.1 billion and operate from 34 branches in Orange and Los Angeles counties in southern California.
